meta.description: Issue taxonomy, cue lexicon (English + Hindi), follow-up question banks, evidence checklists and action-plan templates. Kept separate from application logic so the set can be extended.
meta.evidenceNote: Every evidence item is a document or record that a person can ordinarily obtain or create. Where a listed item depends on a police station, hospital, bank or employer, the workspace states that explicitly rather than assuming it is available.

categories.label: Domestic violence / abuse at home
categories.blurb: Physical, sexual, verbal, emotional or economic abuse by a husband, partner, or relative.
categories.forum: Judicial Magistrate of the First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate (Domestic Violence Act, 2005)
categories.emergency: If there is a risk to life or limb, call the police emergency number 112 first, then consider a protection order.

categories.label: Harassment or molestation
categories.blurb: Unwanted physical contact, sexual demands, lewd comments, stalking or threats.
categories.forum: Police station (for a cognizable offence) or the Magistrate (for a complaint under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita)
categories.emergency: If you are in immediate danger, call 112.

categories.label: Sexual violence
categories.blurb: Rape, attempted rape, molestation with force, or non-consensual sexual contact.
categories.forum: Police station; the medical examination and the FIR are the immediate priorities.
categories.emergency: Call 112. Ask for a woman police officer where one is available.

categories.label: Cybercrime and online abuse
categories.blurb: Fraud, non-consensual imagery, harassment online, threats over messages, or misuse of personal data.
categories.forum: Police station (including the cyber crime unit where one exists) or the nearest Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.
categories.emergency: For an active financial fraud, call 1930 (National Cyber Crime Reporting Helpline) as well as your bank.

categories.label: Workplace harassment
categories.blurb: Harassment by a colleague, manager or employer at the place of work.
categories.forum: Internal Committee at the workplace first; police where the conduct amounts to a cognizable offence.
categories.emergency: The internal route is the statutory first step, but it does not stop you from reporting an offence to the police.

categories.label: Dowry harassment or dowry death
categories.blurb: Demands for dowry or property, or abuse connected with such a demand.
categories.forum: Police station for the offence; Magistrate for a domestic violence application and for maintenance.
categories.emergency: If a demand is accompanied by threats of violence, treat it as an emergency and call 112.

categories.label: Child safety
categories.blurb: Physical or sexual harm to a child, or a duty to report one.
categories.forum: Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police; the report to the Child Welfare Committee follows from there.
categories.emergency: Call 112 or the childline. Reporting is a legal duty on every adult who knows of the offence.

categories.label: Property or housing dispute
categories.blurb: Eviction, trespass, a dispute over a flat, or an unlawful claim over another's property.
categories.forum: Civil court (a rent or possession matter) or the Magistrate (trespass), depending on the claim.
categories.emergency: Do not attempt to take possession yourself; that can convert a civil dispute into a criminal one.

categories.label: Money, loan or recovery
categories.blurb: A bounced cheque, a loan dispute, or recovery pressure including from a guarantor.
categories.forum: Magistrate for a dishonoured cheque; civil court or consumer forum depending on the claim.
categories.emergency: If a recovery agent is threatening you, call 112 and keep the notice.

categories.label: Consumer or service complaint
categories.blurb: A defective product, a deficient service, or a dispute with an online seller.
categories.forum: District / State / National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
categories.emergency: Keep the invoice and every communication with the seller; the consumer route depends on them.

categories.label: Detention, restraint or being confined
categories.blurb: Being held, prevented from leaving, or a relative who has been taken away.
categories.forum: Police station; a habeas corpus petition may be filed before the concerned High Court.
categories.emergency: Call 112 immediately and note the time and place of arrest.

categories.label: Other civil matter
categories.blurb: A dispute that does not fit the categories above.
categories.forum: Civil court in the appropriate jurisdiction.
categories.emergency: If violence or a threat of violence is involved, report that separately to the police.

dateCues.hint: Year — verify what the year refers to

domestic-violence.item: Any written message, SMS or call record that shows the abuse or the demand
Medical records and prescriptions for injuries, or for anxiety and sleep problems
Photographs of injuries, or of damage in the house
domestic-violence.source: take them early, with the date visible if possible

domestic-violence.item: Names and contact details of witnesses — neighbours, relatives, colleagues, domestic help
Marriage invitation, or any document that shows the date and place of the marriage
Proof of residence in the shared household — rent receipt, electricity bill, address proof, or a letter addressed to you at that address
A written statement of what happened, in date order

harassment.item: Screenshots of the messages or comments, with the sender's number or profile visible
Call logs showing repeated calls at particular times
Photographs or video, if taken without risk to your safety
Names of people who witnessed the incident
Medical record, if you were touched or assaulted

sexual-violence.item: A written account of the incident, written down as soon as you are able
Medical examination record — request this early, since the examination is time-sensitive
Preserve the clothes you were wearing on that day, unwashed, in a sealed bag
Any messages, call logs or location history from that period
Names and contact details of anyone who knows where you were and what happened

cyber.item: Screenshots of every relevant message, post or profile, with the URL and date visible
The transaction record, UPI reference number or bank statement for any money you lost
The call recording, if you have one, and the caller's number
The complaint reference or ticket number from the platform's grievance officer
A written note of every step you took and when you took it

workplace-harassment.item: A written complaint to the Internal Committee or the employer, and its acknowledgement
Copies of any email, message or work instruction that relates to the harassment
workplace-harassment.source: your own device or work account

workplace-harassment.item: Your appointment letter and any document describing the reporting structure
Attendance or leave records for the dates of the incidents
Names of colleagues who witnessed the conduct

dowry.item: A written list of every demand made, by whom, when, and in what form
Screenshots or recordings of the demand itself
Records of any property given or demanded — receipts, gift notes, bank transfers, list of items
Medical records if there was any physical harm
Names of witnesses to the demand

child-safety.item: A written account of what you observed or were told, in your own words
The date, place and description of what happened, as precisely as you can recall
The child's account, if the child chooses to give one
Any earlier report you made to a school, an institution or the police

property.item: The agreement, rent receipt or lease, if one exists
Electricity or water bills showing who occupies the premises
Photographs of the premises taken with the date
Any written notice, letter or message from the other party
Any report you made to the police or to the local authority

financial.item: The cheque itself, and the bank-returned memo with the date of return
Proof that you sent the written notice, and the date you sent it
financial.source: registered post or speed post receipt

financial.item: The loan agreement or the surety deed, if you signed one
Any notice received from the lender or a recovery agent

consumer.item: Every email, chat or call record with the seller about the complaint
The complaint reference from the company's grievance officer

liberty.item: The time and place of arrest or detention, and who reported it
The arrest memo or any document produced on release
Hospital records, if there was an injury
The names of anyone who saw the arrest
Any application you filed before a Magistrate or a High Court

civil-other.item: The agreement or contract in writing, if there is one
Proof of payment, or of performance of your side of the contract
Every communication with the other party

domestic-violence: Is there a risk of violence right now, and where would you go tonight if it happened?
Are you living in a shared household with the respondent, and do you have proof of that address?
Did you inform the police or a Protection Officer? If so, is there a diary number?
Are there children in the household, and who currently looks after them day to day?
Is there any financial dependence — a bank account, income or property in your name?
Has anything been demanded in connection with marriage or property, and was it in writing?
harassment: Are the contacts coming from one number or from many?
Has the person been warned once, in writing, that the contact must stop?
Is the person a stranger, an acquaintance, a colleague, or a neighbour?
Do you live or work in the same building or locality as the person?
Has any physical contact happened, and do you have a medical record?
sexual-violence: When was the last time it happened, and has anything happened since?
Has a medical examination been done? If not, how long ago was the incident?
Were you drinking, or were you given anything without your knowledge?
Do you know the full name or description of the person, and can you describe them?
Is there someone you trust who can be present with you while you go to the police station?
cyber: Do you know the account name or the number the messages came from?
Has any money actually moved, and has the bank been informed?
Were any images or videos circulated — who has seen them, and do you know?
Have you already complained to the platform, and do you have a ticket number?
Is there an immediate risk — for example, a threat to disclose something if you do not pay?
workplace-harassment: Does your workplace have an Internal Committee, and do you know its members?
How long ago did the most recent incident occur?
Have you put the complaint in writing, and do you have a copy?
Does the respondent have any reporting authority over you?
Is your job or any condition of it dependent on the respondent's approval?
dowry: Was the demand made before or after the marriage?
Was any demand made in writing, or in front of witnesses?
Has any property already been given, and is there a list or record of it?
Is there any injury or medical record from an incident connected with the demand?
Who else in the household was present when the demand was made?
child-safety: What is the child's age, and what is the relationship to you?
What exactly did you see or hear, and when was the last time?
Has anyone else been told — a teacher, a doctor, a relative?
Is the child currently safe, and who is the child with now?
Do you know the name of the person the child has described?
property: Do you have a written agreement, or is it entirely oral?
Who pays the rent or the utilities, and are they in your name?
Has any notice been served on you, and by what date must you respond?
Is there a police complaint already on record about this property?
Is the dispute with a person living in the premises, or about the right to the property?
financial: Was the cheque returned for insufficiency of funds, and when was it returned?
Did you send a written notice, and was it delivered?
What is the amount of the cheque and the debt it was for?
Did you sign any document as a guarantor or on a hypothecation deed?
Has the lender issued a demand notice, and when?
consumer: What did you pay, and what exactly did the seller promise?
Is the goods defective, or is the service deficient — or both?
Have you complained to the seller or to the company's grievance officer, and when?
How long ago did you buy it, or when did the service fail?
Are you filing for yourself, or on behalf of a group?
liberty: When was the person taken, by whom, and from where?
Was any arrest memo or receipt given?
Has the person been produced before a Magistrate, and if so, when?
Is there a place of last known residence or work?
Is there any risk to life, and is anyone dependent on that person?
civil-other: Is there a written contract or agreement?
What remedy are you actually looking for — payment, return of property, or an order?
Has any limitation period notice been received, or any demand letter?
Has the other party responded to any written notice from you?
Is there a parallel proceeding already on foot anywhere?

referralChannels.name: Police emergency number
referralChannels.when: Immediate danger to life, liberty or personal safety, including domestic violence in progress.
referralChannels.note: Works from any phone in India, including without a SIM, on supported networks.

referralChannels.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Helpline
referralChannels.when: Online financial fraud, or a cybercrime in progress. Available 24 hours.
referralChannels.note: Call the helpline and also file on the cybercrime portal, because the portal generates a reference number you will need.

referralChannels.name: National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
referralChannels.when: Any cybercrime, including non-consensual imagery, online threats and fraud.
referralChannels.note: File here to obtain an acknowledgement and a reference number, then report at the police station.

referralChannels.name: National Legal Services Authority
referralChannels.when: You need a free lawyer, or you need to reach the Legal Services Authority in your state.
referralChannels.note: NALSA coordinates the District Legal Services Authorities. Free legal aid is available to women and children in need of protection under section 12(c) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

referralChannels.name: District Legal Services Authority
referralChannels.when: You appear in person and need a lawyer appointed for you.
referralChannels.note: Every district has a DLSA with a legal services clinic and a lok adalat system. Ask the court clerk for the Legal Services Cell.

referralChannels.name: NALSA helpline
referralChannels.when: General guidance on obtaining legal aid.
referralChannels.note: Availability may vary by state; confirm on the NALSA website before relying on it.

referralChannels.name: Women helpline
referralChannels.when: A woman needs support relating to violence, harassment or safety.
referralChannels.note: A support and referral service operated by the states; it is not a substitute for the police in an emergency.

referralChannels.name: Childline
referralChannels.when: A child is at risk or needs protection.

referralChannels.name: National Commission for Women
referralChannels.when: You need to lodge a complaint about a violation of a woman's rights, or need guidance.
referralChannels.note: The NCW can take up certain matters, but it is not a substitute for a complaint to the police or a court.

referralChannels.name: National Consumer Helpline
referralChannels.when: A consumer complaint that has not been resolved by the company.
referralChannels.note: A precursor to filing before a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission; keep the company's reference number.

referralChannels.name: e-Daakhil, National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
referralChannels.note: A complaint can also be filed in person at the District Commission.
